title: Jours, dates, saisons et durées
summary: Give dates, distinguish a particular day from a regular habit, and choose between time units and duration-focused words.
objectives: Name days, months and seasons and give a date.
Use le with repeated days and the weekend.
Distinguish an/année, jour/journée, matin/matinée and soir/soirée without false absolute rules.

sections.title: French dates normally use day + month, without an English ordinal ending
paragraphs: The days are lundi, mardi, mercredi, jeudi, vendredi, samedi, dimanche. The months are janvier, février, mars, avril, mai, juin, juillet, août, septembre, octobre, novembre, décembre. These names normally have no capital in French except at the start of a sentence. Days and months are masculine nouns when an article is needed: un lundi, le mois de mai.

For a calendar date use le + cardinal day + month: le deux avril. The first is le premier, not le un. With digits: le 1er avril, le 2 avril. You can answer On est le… or Nous sommes le… . For a month without a specific date use en: en juillet. A year also commonly takes en: en 2026. Do not add de between the date number and the month.
points: French numeric date order is normally day/month/year; writing the month name avoids international ambiguity.

examples.english: It is the first of April.
examples.note: Only the first uses premier in ordinary dates.

examples.english: The course starts on the twelfth of September.

examples.note: A month alone usually takes en.

mistakes.why: Ordinary French dates do not insert de before the month.

sections.title: A definite article can turn a day into a regular habit
paragraphs: Without an article, lundi often refers to one particular Monday understood from context. Le lundi normally means on Mondays or every Monday. Lundi prochain means next Monday; lundi dernier means last Monday. Le week-end often means at weekends, while ce week-end means this weekend. Week-end and the rectified weekend are both accepted spellings; la fin de semaine is the common Canadian term.

The seasons are le printemps (m., spring), l'été (m., summer), l'automne (m., autumn/fall), l'hiver (m., winter). For in a season, use au printemps but en été, en automne, en hiver. In a general or recurring time phrase, the season can also have the definite article: l'été, je travaille dehors. As a subject, it takes its article: l'hiver est long.
points: Le can mean a habitual occasion, not only a previously identified object.

examples.english: The flowers come back in spring.

examples.french: Nous voyageons **en été**, mais **l'hiver**, nous restons chez nous.
examples.english: We travel in summer, but in winter we stay at home.
examples.note: En and a definite-article time phrase are both possible patterns.

mistakes.why: The established seasonal construction is au printemps.

sections.title: A unit count and a lived period are different viewpoints
paragraphs: Un an, un jour, un matin and un soir are masculine. Une année, une journée, une matinée and une soirée are feminine. The shorter words often count units or name a point in the calendar; the longer words often emphasise the period's duration, contents or experience. Age normally uses ans: j'ai trente ans. Bonne année ! is the conventional New Year wish.

Use demain matin or ce soir to locate an event. Use toute la matinée or toute la soirée when emphasising the whole period. Bonjour is a greeting; bonne journée is a wish for the day ahead. Bonsoir greets someone in the evening; bonne soirée wishes them a pleasant evening.

This is not a strict rule that numbers always require an and never année. Deux années difficiles is natural when describing those years' experience. L'an prochain and l'année prochaine both mean next year; dernier/prochain agree with the chosen noun. Learn the perspective and the established expressions, not a mechanical English-year substitution.
points: Tout/toute in the examples means the whole period and agrees with its noun.

examples.english: I am thirty years old. It is an important year.
examples.note: Age counts units; the second sentence describes a period.

examples.french: Elle part demain **matin** et travaille toute la **matinée**.
examples.english: She leaves tomorrow morning and works all morning.
examples.note: A time point contrasts with duration.

examples.french: Il vient ce **soir** et reste toute la **soirée**.
examples.english: He is coming this evening and staying all evening.
examples.note: The longer form focuses on the period.

examples.english: We are staying three days. Have a good day!
examples.note: A unit count contrasts with a conventional wish.

examples.french: L'**an prochain**, ou l'**année prochaine**, je voyage.
examples.english: Next year, or next year, I am travelling.
examples.note: Both phrases are correct; agreement changes with the noun.

mistakes.why: For ordinary age, use ans, not années.
Matinée is feminine, so the article is la.

sections.title: Look beyond le before deciding that a day repeats
paragraphs: Le jeudi on its own in a timetable commonly describes a weekly habit. Add a full calendar date and le jeudi 18 juin names a single dated day instead. The article also belongs with the day when you discuss it as a category or subject. Do not translate every le + weekday mechanically as every.

examples.english: The drop-in session takes place on Thursdays.

examples.french: La permanence exceptionnelle a lieu **le jeudi 18 juin**.
examples.english: The special drop-in session takes place on Thursday 18 June.
examples.note: The full date singles out one occurrence.

examples.french: **Le jeudi** est mon jour le plus chargé.
examples.note: The weekday is the sentence subject, considered generally.

practice.prompt: Does 'L'inscription ouvre le vendredi 6 novembre' identify a dated opening or a weekly opening?
practice.explanation: The calendar date prevents interpreting le vendredi here as every Friday.

practice.prompt: Complete the full dated expression: 'Le tournoi commence ___ samedi 12 décembre.' Supply the article.
practice.explanation: A weekday with its full date normally takes le, without implying repetition.

practice.prompt: Add the missing article before a weekday used as the subject: '___ mardi est une journée calme au musée.'
practice.explanation: Le mardi is a day considered generally and is the sentence subject.

practice.prompt: Write April 1 in French words, beginning with le.
Supply le or aucun for a habit: 'Je travaille ___ mardi' means I work every Tuesday.
practice.explanation: Le mardi marks the recurring day.

practice.prompt: Supply ans or années for ordinary age: 'Elle a quarante ___.'
Write May 8 in French words, beginning with le.
practice.explanation: Except the first, ordinary dates use cardinals.

practice.prompt: Supply the preposition: 'Le festival est ___ août.'
Supply the article for a recurring weekend habit: '___ week-end, elle se repose.'
practice.explanation: Le week-end can mean at weekends.

practice.prompt: Supply the preposition: 'Il fait froid ___ hiver.'
practice.explanation: The fixed seasonal phrase is en hiver.

practice.prompt: Supply the preposition: 'Les feuilles tombent ___ automne.'
Supply matin or matinée: 'Je viens demain ___.'
Supply soir or soirée: 'Elle danse toute la ___.'
practice.explanation: Toute la soirée emphasises the full period and is feminine.

practice.prompt: Supply jour or journée in the conventional farewell: 'Bonne ___ !'
practice.explanation: Bonne journée wishes someone a pleasant day.

practice.prompt: Supply an or année in the conventional New Year wish: 'Bonne ___ !'
practice.explanation: The established wish uses feminine année.

practice.prompt: Supply the definite article for a recurring summer habit: '___ été, je travaille dehors.'
practice.explanation: L'été is an alternative seasonal time phrase.

practice.prompt: Can 'deux années difficiles' be grammatical even though it contains a number?
practice.explanation: Années can emphasise the experience of the periods; the distinction is not an absolute numbers rule.

production_task.prompt: Write a short calendar note: one exact date, one weekly habit, one seasonal activity and a wish for someone's day.
production_task.model_answer: Le cours commence le deux octobre. Je travaille le mercredi. En hiver, je lis le soir. Bonne journée !
production_task.translation: The class starts on the second of October. I work on Wednesdays. In winter, I read in the evening. Have a good day!
rubric: Use a cardinal date except for the first.
Use le for the recurring weekday.
Use journée in the farewell wish.
